body.p: Claims 1-2, 4-15, and 17-20 will be pending after entry of the present paper. Claims 1, 8, 10, 11, 15, 17, and 19 are amended. Support for the amendments may be found in the originally filed specification, drawings, and claims. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of this application in view of the amendments and remarks submitted herein.

The Examiner rejects 1-5, 9-11, 14-16, and 20 under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over U.S. PG Pub. 2020/0164988 (Alvarez) in view of U.S. PG Pub. 2022/0111087 (Childress), further in view of CN 112153991 (Baarman). Applicant respectfully disagrees; however, Applicant amends independent claims 1, 10, and 15 solely to expedite prosecution.

Alvarez is directed towards "lavatory occupancy detection systems and methods" (Title). "The occupancy detection control unit is configured to determine an occupancy status of the lavatory based on the door sensor signal and the presence sensor signal(s)" (Abstract). Nowhere in Alvarez is it disclosed or contemplated that the "the central controller configured to: control the toilet seat of the lavatory in response to receiving the request to lift the toilet seat, control the toilet lid of the lavatory in response to receiving the request to lift the toilet lid, control dispensing of the soap from a soap dispenser in response to receiving the request to dispense the soap within the lavatory, control operation of the faucet in response to receiving the faucet request, control flushing of the toilet of the lavatory in response to receiving the flush request, control the trash flap in response to receiving the trash flap request" in combination with the remaining limitations of independent claim 1 as amended.

As outlined in [0002] of the present disclosure, '[c]onventional aircraft lavatories include numerous electronic functions such as a toilet flush, sink water flowing, lighting, and signage that each have individual controllers and power sources. This results in circuit breaker sizing and wiring to each function to be oversized in order to compensate for worst-case scenarios in which each function is operating simultaneously. When an aircraft operator desires to add additional functions (such as a new light source), the addition may result in significant rewiring of the lavatory, extra weight added to the aircraft, and extra power draw because a new controller will also be installed." The claimed invention addresses this by having a "central controller" with the functionality claimed in independent claims 1, namely, the central controller is configured to control each element claimed

above. In contrast, the "control unit" from Alvarez controls the cleaning lights and the sanitization lights, as indicated by the Examiner in the Office Action, p. 2, and does not "control the toil seat," "control the toilet lid," "control dispensing of the soap," "control operation of the faucet," and/or "control flushing of the toilet as claimed." Applicant further asserts that the remaining cited references fail to cure the deficiencies of Alvarez. Therefore, Applicant asserts that the rejection should be withdrawn and claim 1 is in condition for allowance.

Similarly, Alvarez fails to disclose or contemplate at least "each of the multiple actuators associated with a respective sensor in the multiple sensors" and "the central controller configured to: receive a request from each of the multiple sensors located in the lavatory; responsive to receiving the request from a first of the multiple sensors, performing, via one of the multiple actuators associated with the first of the multiple sensors, the first action that corresponds to the first of the multiple sensors" (emphasis added), in combination with the remaining limitations of amended independent claim 10. More specifically, the Examiner indicates that "an actuator located in the lavatory and configured to perform a first action" reads on the "actuator 936 which actuates or turns on UV light 910 for a or first action as shown in figure 11, or the actuators in the detection control unit 114 which control cleaning of the lavatory as disclosed n paragraphs 43 and 44 and actuation of the lights in figure 10 indicating the occupancy status plus actuation of the UV light 910)" (Office Action, p. 2). However, these "actuators" are not "associated with a respective sensor in the multiple sensors as claimed." The actuators actuate based on data received from multiple sensors after determining an occupancy of the lavatory. In contrast, claim 10 recites "responsive to receiving the request from a first of the multiple sensors, performing, via one of the multiple actuators associated with the first of the multiple sensors, the first action that corresponds to the first of the multiple sensors" (emphasis added). Furthermore, the remaining cited references fail to cure the deficiencies of Alvarez. Accordingly, Applicant asserts that the rejection should be withdrawn and claim 10 is in condition for allowance.
Similarly, Alvarez fails to disclose or contemplate at least "receiving, by a central controller and from a first of a plurality of touchless sensors disposed in the lavatory, a request to perform an

action, control, by the central controller and via a first of a plurality of actuators, the action associated with the first of the plurality of touchless sensors; receiving, by at least one sensor of the lavatory, data corresponding to the lavatory, the data including the request to perform the action" (emphasis added), in combination with the remaining limitations of amended independent claim 15. More specifically, as outlined about, "the action" in Alvarez is not "associated with the first of the plurality of touchless sensors" as claimed, nor the "data corresponding to the lavatory" from Alvarez "including the request to perform the action" (emphasis added) as claimed. Furthermore, the remaining cited references fail to cure the deficiencies of Alvarez. Accordingly, Applicant asserts that the rejection should be withdrawn and claim 15 is in condition for allowance

The Examiner further rejects claims 6, 7, 12, 17, and 18 under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Alvarez in view of Childress, in view of Baarman, further in view of U.S. PG Pub. 2018/0369434 (Callaghan). Claims 6 and 7 depend from claim 1, claim 12 depends from claim 10, and claims 17 and 18 depend from claim 15. Applicant asserts that Callaghan fails to cure the deficiencies of Alvarez, Childress, and Baarman. Therefore, Applicant asserts that the rejection should be withdrawn and the claims are in condition for allowance.

The Examiner further rejects claim 8, 13, and 19 under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Alvarez in view of Childress, in view of Baarman, further in view of U.S. PG Pub. 2008/0131332 (Nguyen). Claim 8 depends from claim 1, claim 13 depends from claim 10, and claim 19 depends from claim 15. Applicant asserts that Nguyen fails to cure the deficiencies of Alvarez, Childress, and Baarman. Therefore, Applicant asserts that the rejection should be withdrawn and the claims are in condition for allowance.

In view of the above remarks and amendments, Applicant respectfully submits that all pending claims are in condition for allowance. The Examiner is invited to telephone the undersigned at the Examiner's convenience, if doing so will further prosecution of the subject application. The Commissioner is hereby authorized to charge any fees that may be required or credit any overpayment to Deposit Account No. 192814. This statement does NOT authorize charge of the issue fee.
Respectfully submitted, Date: November 25, 2024 By: /Gregg Scheiferstein/
